note: My hedge thesis says that in the worlds where the primary loses, voters rally behind the establishment across Europe: German federal politics steadies, Bund, euro and DAX risk pricing improves, and French RN polling softens. None of the candidates carries that mechanism. The German, French and euro-rates exposures are missing entirely. The nearest candidates are the Clacton by-election markets (E6 winner, E14 Farage vote share). They fail as hedges for three reasons. First, the vote is driven by local factors in one UK constituency. Second, its date is unknown and may fall long after September. Third, Farage winning his own seat back does not depend on whether eastern German voters tactically back the CDU or SPD. The Rhine level (E9) is a German instrument but depends on hydrology, not politics. The crypto markets, Fed markets, US primaries, Russian Duma and war markets have no causal link to AfD seat counts. Any claim tying them to C3 would be a claim I would not stand behind, so I record no instrument.
